NBA Prop Reversion Study

NBA player props · 2022-23 to 2025-26 · real sportsbook lines

Does an over predict an under?

No. After a player goes over his line, the under hits 51.0% to 52.8% of the time next game for points, rebounds and assists. After an under, it hits 51.3% to 52.2%. Last game's result shifts the next one by less than 0.6 percentage points.

Steals and blocks look like the opposite of the thesis in the raw numbers: unders hit less often after an over. The odds already account for that. Compared against each bet's own price, last game's result adds about nothing in any of the five stats.

The direct test

Each player-game is graded once, against the median line across books (the closing line where the feed has a real one, otherwise the opener). Blue is how often the under hit when the player went under last game; orange, when he went over. If the thesis were right, every orange dot would sit well to the right of its blue dot.

Steals and blocks lines sit at 0.5 or 1.5 and are priced through the juice, so raw hit rates mix players the books price very differently. The fair comparison is against the odds: did unders beat their price-implied chance by more after an over than after an under?

Streaks

Maybe one over isn't enough and the bounce comes after a run. These panels bet against streaks of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6+ games at a single book's closing line. Long streaks are rare, so the right side of each panel rests on a few hundred bets.

What the books do after a big game

After a big game the books raise the next line by about 0.10 to 0.12 standard deviations for every SD the player beat his last line by. For points, rebounds and assists the next result then lands right on the new line (slopes −0.002 to +0.009, none statistically different from zero). The thesis needs the books to overreact. They don't. For steals, blocks and 3-pointers made, results carry past the new line, the opposite of what the thesis needs (the odds, not the line, absorb most of it).

95% intervals, clustered by player. SD is the player's own, over his previous 20 games.

Twenty-four seasons of box scores

Prop lines only go back to 2022-23. To see whether the stats themselves bounce back, this uses each player's trailing 10-game average as a stand-in line for every season since 2002-03. A placebo that shuffles game order within each player-season removes the small mechanical effect of the average including the last game. Above zero would mean stats really do fall back after an above-average game.

In 72 of 72 season-stat pairs across 24 seasons, the opposite of reversal shows up: an above-average game makes the next game more likely to be above average too, by 2.8 percentage points on average for points, rebounds and assists. Roles and minutes carry over from game to game.

No book sets lines this naively. This section is about the stats, not about betting.

The thesis as a bet

Betting it anyway on all five stats, against last game's result at a single book's closing line: 179,629 bets, a 48.9% hit rate against 52.2% needed, and −6.4% on every dollar staked. Shopping the best opening line across every book in the feed only trims the loss to −3.4%.

Each row bets the opposite of the player's last result against his line: 1 unit a bet at the real price, pushes refunded, props for players who sat out void. “Needed” is the hit rate that breaks even at the prices actually taken.

Searching every variation

Across 16,700 strategy variants, the best on 2022-23 to 2024-25 was “Every under in the regular season · Rebounds · opening line · best line”: +3.6% on 36,037 bets. That is more than luck alone would produce from this many tries (Reality Check p = 0.01). But it depends on shopping every book's line: at a single book the same bet returned −0.8% over the same seasons. On 2025-26, which it never saw, it returned −4.2% on 3,933 bets. 128 strategies pass a 10% false-discovery screen on the earlier seasons, and 125 of them are versions of one bet: shopping every book's opening line, mostly on unders. Together they returned −4.0% on 2025-26, and 14% of them made money.

Every strategy was ranked on 2022-23 to 2024-25 and then scored on 2025-26. A real edge would put points along the diagonal. Strategies that looked best on the past instead fall back to zero or below, which is what overfitting looks like.

Baselines: every over, every under

Unders lose less than overs: −3.4% against −9.6% at a single book's close across the five core stats. That's the familiar lean of prop markets, and it explains why every “bet the under after…” idea looks better than its “bet the over” twin. It still doesn't beat the vig at one book.

The data

Box scores, schedules, game lines and player props all come from ESPN's public JSON APIs. For every game, the prop feed keeps each sportsbook's opening and last-recorded line and price. Players are matched to box scores by ESPN athlete id.

Main prop lines by season and book

Which lines can be trusted

Some of the feed's “closing” lines were recorded during the game, and one season's openers are full of placeholder prices. Each book-season is scored against a yardstick that knows nothing about the game: the player's trailing 10-game average. Real lines miss by about 93-98% as much as that average. A close that misses far less was captured in-game; an opener that misses more than the average is junk. Flagged lines are dropped, and the rest of that book-season is kept.

Inferred over/under labels

DraftKings' 2025-26 lines arrive without side labels, so they are read in the order every labeled book uses (over first, 99.98% of the time). A slope near 1 means the implied probabilities match what happened; flipped labels would give a negative slope.

Method and limits

  • “Previous game” is the player's previous game played in the same season. A game with no posted line breaks a streak.
  • Strategies bet 1 unit at the real American odds. Pushes are refunded, and props for players who sat out are void.
  • “Best line” takes the lowest line on offer for overs and the highest for unders, then the better price. It assumes every book's line was available at once, so treat it as an upper bound. “Single book” sends every bet to one major book.
  • Opening-line bets use only what was known at the open. Closing-line bets may also use the open-to-close move.
  • Coverage: four seasons of props. 2025-26 has props for only 400 of 1,322 games, because the feed kept DraftKings props for some games only after ESPN switched books in December 2025. FanDuel and offshore books are not in the feed, and there is no intraday line history.
  • Results assume you could get the posted price. Books limit winning prop bettors quickly.
